# Combat turns and actions

## Turn structure and action economy
Combat cycles through rounds in initiative order. On its turn, a creature may move up to its Speed and take one action, in either order, and may split movement around actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions taken on that turn. Brief speech and gestures cost neither action nor movement. One object or environmental feature may be interacted with for free during the move or action; a second normally needs Utilize. A Bonus Action exists only when a rule grants it, at most one per turn. A Reaction is an immediate triggered response, at most one until the start of that creature's next turn. Never waste the action: if no attack or feature helps, consider Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide, Ready, Search, Study, or Utilize as the situation allows.

## Initiative, surprise, and delaying
Initiative fixes the turn order from round to round; identical monsters may share one roll. A creature surprised when combat starts has Disadvantage on its Initiative roll. The SRD has no general rule for moving a turn later in the initiative order: Ready can defer one specified action or movement to a perceivable trigger by spending the action now and the Reaction later; Dodge is the defensive fallback.

## Monster turns, Multiattack, and Legendary Actions
A monster can use universal actions and the actions, Bonus Actions, and Reactions in its stat block. Multiattack is a listed way to make its specified attacks and use any additional abilities included in that entry as part of the Attack action. Legendary Actions are listed stat-block actions taken one at a time immediately after another creature's turn; they spend the monster's limited uses, cannot be taken while Incapacitated or unable to act, and all uses return at the start of its turn.
